record.title: Apex Math is credited in a preprint with a proof of Mockenhaupt’s majorant conjecture
record.summary: A paper submitted to arXiv on 9 September 2026 reports an analytic proof of Mockenhaupt’s three-term Hardy–Littlewood majorant conjecture. Its v2 appendix says the mathematical argument was produced by Apex Math, names Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, and says the authors read and verified the proof and accept responsibility. The authors’ argument covers integer k≥4, including the previously open cases k≥6; the appendix details four AI-output errors and corrections, says no formal verification was completed, and describes exact-arithmetic checks only for a finite range. the research desk did not independently check the proof.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report an analytic proof of Mockenhaupt’s three-term Hardy–Littlewood majorant conjecture for every integer k≥4 and 2k<p<2k+2, covering the previously open cases k≥6; cases k≤5 were already known.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The v2 paper states that its mathematical argument was produced by Apex Math, an auto-research system built by the authors, and names Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol as the underlying language models. The authors say they read and verified the argument and take responsibility for it.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper’s Appendix A documents four identifiable AI-output errors and their corrections, reports exact-arithmetic machine checks for a finite range, and states that the Lean 4 formalization attempt is incomplete and that no formal verification is claimed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Apex Intelligence’s 16 September 2026 company release separately claimed that its AI system produced a complete proof of a majorization conjecture but did not name the conjecture or link the paper. The arXiv preprint identifies the specific result; the release alone does not establish the proof’s correctness.

evidence_gaps.description: The theorem and AI attribution are described in a detailed author preprint, but no independent specialist assessment of the full proof was located.
The authors report an incomplete Lean formalization; ancillary scripts verify only finite-range computations and are not the proof.
No complete public execution log or independent audit of Apex Math’s contribution and human/system division of work was located.

brief.importance_rationale: If the stated proof is correct, completing the previously open cases of a long-standing harmonic-analysis conjecture with an argument attributed to an AI research system would materially affect research priorities in AI-for-math and mathematical analysis. A 6 reflects a major but theorem-specific result; independent specialist review and formal verification are absent, and authors report substantial human review and correction.
limitations: The proof’s correctness and novelty have not been independently assessed in this review; the authors’ claim that they verified it remains attributed first-party evidence.
The paper concerns one theorem in harmonic analysis. It does not establish general mathematical research ability, autonomous publication, or general recursive self-improvement.
The authors attribute the mathematical argument to Apex Math and name Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, but do not provide a complete external run log or independent attribution audit.
Appendix A reports four identifiable system errors and corrections. This is useful process disclosure, but also shows that drafts required substantial checking and repair.
Exact-arithmetic scripts recheck a finite range and are not the proof; the attempted Lean 4 formalization is incomplete, and no formal verification is claimed.

The 16 September company release describes an unnamed “majorization conjecture” without linking this paper. The paper and its AI-use appendix resolve the specific result, but the press release alone did not.
brief.summary: A paper submitted to arXiv on 9 September 2026 reports an analytic proof of Mockenhaupt’s three-term Hardy–Littlewood majorant conjecture. Its v2 appendix says the mathematical argument was produced by Apex Math, names Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, and says the authors read and verified the proof and accept responsibility. The authors’ argument covers integer k≥4, including the previously open cases k≥6; the appendix details four AI-output errors and corrections, says no formal verification was completed, and describes exact-arithmetic checks only for a finite range. the research desk did not independently check the proof.

technical.claimed_result: The authors claim that for each integer k≥4 and every real p with 2k<p<2k+2, the Lp norm of 1+e(x)−e((k+2)x) exceeds that of 1+e(x)+e((k+2)x), thereby settling all previously open cases k≥6 when combined with known results for k≤5. They attribute production of the mathematical argument to Apex Math.
technical.demonstrated_result: the research desk did not independently demonstrate the theorem or verify the proof. The primary arXiv source contains a self-contained analytic argument, a theorem statement, an explicit AI-use attribution and a detailed account of author-reported verification and system errors/corrections.
technical.mechanism: The paper reduces the norm comparison to positivity of a sum of resonant Fourier coefficients. It represents those coefficients through analytically continued triple-Bessel integrals, derives a positive lower bound for the leading mode, and bounds the remaining odd modes by a uniform tail estimate. Appendix A attributes the mathematical argument to an AI research system; the paper says authors verified the argument and documents machine checks for a finite range.
technical.regime: A single theorem in harmonic analysis on the torus: for integer k≥4 and real p strictly between 2k and 2k+2, compare the Lp norms of two three-term trigonometric polynomials differing by one sign. Earlier work supplies cases k≤5. The claim does not measure general mathematical problem-solving or self-improvement.
technical.reproducibility: The paper provides a self-contained analytic argument and ancillary scripts for finite-range checks. The authors say they read and verified the proof, but the research desk did not independently inspect every step or run the scripts. The paper explicitly says Lean 4 formalization is incomplete and does not claim formal verification.
technical.strongest_baseline: Prior mathematical literature had established cases k≤5; the paper claims one analytic argument covering all k≥4, including the previously open range k≥6. No matched AI-system or human mathematician performance baseline is presented.

brief.title: Apex Math is credited in a preprint with a proof of Mockenhaupt’s majorant conjecture
brief.why_it_matters: If the proof is correct, an AI research system contributed to an analytic result in harmonic analysis that resolves the remaining integer cases of a long-standing conjecture. This is evidence about one specific theorem and a human-authored, human-verified paper; it does not establish general mathematical research capability or independently validated AI autonomy.
